cards.text: Hosea, a prophet (Hosea 1:1), brings the LORD's message about Ephraim, one of the tribes of Israel (Numbers 1:33). When Ephraim spoke, there was TREMBLING, and he was exalted in Israel. Me? When I talked in the junk drawer I spent years in, the rubber bands just yawned.

cards.question: Ephraim was exalted in Israel. But then he incurred guilt, and he died. What did Ephraim incur guilt through?

cards.text: And it doesn't stop there: now they sin more and more, making cast images out of their own silver. FIVE-STAR materials, zero-star idea.

cards.question: The people are making idols out of their own silver. True or false: these idols are the work of craftsmen.

cards.text: Skillfully made, too, and people say of them, "They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!" So where does chasing idols get them?

cards.question: They'll be like the morning mist, like early dew, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, and like smoke through an open window. What do all four pictures have in common?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: "Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me."

cards.question: The LORD goes way back with His people, all the way to Egypt. He says He knew them in the ___, in the land of drought.

cards.text: Then they get pasture, and when they have pasture, they're satisfied. Full, comfy, feet up, like me after taste-testing a WHOLE bowl of chocolate chip dough.

cards.question: Once the people are satisfied in their pasture, their hearts become proud. What happens as a result?

cards.text: So the LORD says like a lion He will pounce on them, like a leopard He will lurk by the path, and like a wild beast He will tear them apart.

cards.question: One more animal joins the lion and the leopard. The LORD says He will attack them like a ___ robbed of her cubs.

cards.text: After all those wild animals, the LORD drops the pictures and talks straight to Israel. Just the truth, and it lands harder than a rolling pin off the top shelf.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel they are destroyed. Why does He say it happened?

answers.text: Their king lost a great battle

cards.text: Then the LORD asks where their king is now to save them, along with the rulers they told, "Give me a king and princes". It's like hiring the guy who swore he'd fix everything, and the night the storm hits, he's not picking up.

cards.question: The LORD talks about the king Israel asked for. True or false: the LORD says He gave Israel a king as a reward.

cards.text: In His anger He gave them a king, and in His wrath He took him away. And Ephraim's sin is bound up and stored up, the one box in the whole bakery I would NEVER want to open.

cards.question: Labor pains come upon Ephraim, but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, what does he do?

answers.text: He fails to present himself at birth
He is born into a king's house
He is born holding his brother's heel

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of all this, the LORD says, "Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting?"

cards.question: Just before the LORD asks Death and Sheol those questions, what does He say He will do?

cards.text: Then He says, "Compassion is hidden from My eyes." Ephraim may be flourishing among his brothers, but a wind is coming.

cards.question: The east wind that will come is a wind from ___, rising up from the desert.
True or false: when the east wind comes, Ephraim's spring runs dry.

cards.text: His fountain fails too, and the wind plunders his treasury of every precious article. Then the message turns to Samaria, a city of Israel (1 Kings 16:24).

cards.question: Samaria will bear her guilt. Why?

cards.text: This part is heavy. They will fall by the sword, their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.
